verdict.rationale: HelixDB has a documented multi-tenancy guide that discusses three isolation levels. Helix Cloud's own approach is row-level isolation, with the tenancy model implemented at the application layer rather than through native namespaces, partitions, or per-tenant collections. Separate databases can be created per project, but nothing shows this is cheap at many-tenant scale, and the documented limits cover only rate, burst and query budgets. Missing for 10: native namespace/partition/collection primitives, documented tenant-count or per-tenant capacity limits, evidence of cheap isolation at scale, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can isolate many tenants cheaply using namespaces, partitions, or per-tenant collections with documented limits

citations.quote: Helix Cloud focuses on row-level isolation, which lets you implement any tenancy model at the application layer without structural constraints on the database.
Multi-tenant architectures generally fall into one of three isolation levels.
Database-specific overrides can change the sustained rate, burst capacity, and query attempt budget.
